title: Scholialang Skills 02: public positive, negative, composition, and installed-artifact verification
problem: Version and source parity do not prove that advertised functionality works. A prior public plugin could create DAG records yet fail its own export/lint lifecycle because individual features were tested without positive, negative, composition, and installed-artifact coverage. Users need one deterministic verification workflow that tests the public contract rather than merely comparing versions.
outcome: The public repository contains a concise scholialang-verify skill backed by a deterministic runner. It executes bounded shared positive/negative fixtures, DAG create/add/link/finish/export/parse/validate round trips, action-to-finding and hypothesis-evidence-finding closure, catalog completeness, search/neighbors/compaction smoke, and clean installed wheel/plugin probes. It emits per-scenario machine evidence and an honest overall verdict without mutating the user's real DAG store.
hard_constraints: Initialize the new skill with the system skill-creator init script and use the same canonical-source/materialization convention established by Skills 01. Do not create auxiliary README/install/changelog files inside it.

All verification must run against isolated temporary repositories, DAG databases, homes, and virtual environments. Never write to the user's real ~/.scholialang database, plugin cache, or project traces.

Parity is one facet only. The required matrix includes at least one positive, meaningful negative, composition/round-trip, and clean installed-artifact scenario for every advertised feature family in scope.
Exercise the actual public MCP tool/lifecycle boundary where possible; do not replace an end-to-end check with direct calls to private helpers and then claim protocol functionality.
Preserve raw request/response/result artifacts within bounded redacted evidence. Do not retain secrets, customer data, hidden reasoning, or unrestricted home-directory snapshots.
A skipped required scenario is not pass. Distinguish pass, fail, unsupported, and not_run, and require all declared required scenarios for an overall pass.

Reuse shared scholialang-spec fixtures when present and clearly report when the sibling fixture source is unavailable. The installed-artifact arm must remain independently runnable from a clean source tree or wheel fixture.

Run the new verification suite plus existing MCP protocol, support-matrix, release-version, vendored-contract, and Claude Desktop bundle tests. No version bump, publication, tag, global install, or default-branch mutation.
success_metrics: The verifier produces deterministic scenario JSON with pass/fail/unsupported/not_run and an overall verdict derived only from required scenarios.
Positive and negative fixtures cover catalog, Goal/Concluding, Action/Finding, Hypothesis/Evidence/Finding, and invalid unknown-kind/reference cases.
A full isolated DAG lifecycle exports parseable/valid Scholia and exercises search, neighbors, and compaction without touching the real store.
A clean installed-artifact arm and at least one vendored plugin arm pass the same required contract.

stories.title: Define the bounded conformance scenario manifest and evidence schema
stories.description: Create an explicit scenario manifest with required/optional status, public boundary, inputs, expected outcome, evidence paths, and deterministic verdict derivation. Include positive, negative, composition, and installed-artifact classes.

stories.title: Create the isolated scholialang-verify runner and skill
stories.description: Build the skill and isolated runner around temporary homes, stores and environments. Exercise public MCP and CLI boundaries, shared fixtures, full DAG round trips, and installed artifacts.

stories.title: Pin failure honesty, determinism, and no-real-store tests
stories.description: Test required skip/failure behavior, stable repeated evidence, redaction, hostile environment isolation, and a sentinel real DAG store that remains byte-unmodified. Re-run the existing contract suites.
